title: Syntax, Indentation & Common Errors
description: Understand Python’s strict formatting rules and how to decode error messages.

slides.title: Why Syntax Matters 💢
slides.content:
# Python is a Grammar Nazi

Every language has rules. In Python:
* **Indentation** defines blocks of code (no curly braces `{}`)
* Colons `:` start a new block
* Case sensitivity (`name` vs `Name`)

Violate them, and Python yells at you. Let's learn the rules so you can yell back.

slides.title: The Holy Indentation Rule 📏
slides.content:
# Use 4 Spaces (Not Tabs!)

```python
if True:
    print("This is indented")
print("This is back to normal")
```
* The `if` line ends with `:`
* The next line **must** be indented more than the `if`
* All lines in the block must have the **exact same** indentation

**Stick to 4 spaces per level.** Your editor can convert tabs to spaces.

slides.title: Indentation Example
slides.codeSnippet:
x = 10
if x > 5:
    print("x is big")
    print("inside the if")
print("outside")

quizData.question: What happens if you mix tabs and spaces for indentation?

options.text: You'll get a TabError or inconsistent indentation
The code runs fine as long as it looks aligned

quizData.explanation: Python 3 disallows mixing tabs and spaces. Always use spaces (or configure your editor to insert spaces when you press Tab).

slides.title: Comments & Blank Lines 📄
slides.content:
# Whitespace That Doesn't Hurt

* Blank lines are ignored – use them to separate logical sections
* Comments (`#`) are ignored
* You can indent comments to align with code:
```python
if True:
    # explain the next line
    print("Got it")
```

slides.title: Case Sensitivity
slides.content:
# `Print` is not `print`

Python distinguishes uppercase and lowercase:
```python
print("works")
Print("Error")  # NameError: name 'Print' is not defined
```
Most built‑in functions are lowercase. Variable names are case‑sensitive too.

quizData.question: The variable `hack` and `Hack` refer to the same location in memory.
quizData.explanation: Python treats uppercase and lowercase letters as different. `hack` and `Hack` are two distinct variables.

slides.title: Reading Error Messages 🔍
slides.content:
# Don't Panic – Read the Traceback

When an error occurs, Python shows a traceback:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "myscript.py", line 3, in <module>
    print(undefined_var)
NameError: name 'undefined_var' is not defined
```
It tells you:
* The file and line number
* The type of error (NameError, SyntaxError, etc.)
* A description

**Always start at the bottom line** – that's the actual error.

slides.title: Common Error Types
slides.codeSnippet:
# SyntaxError: missing punctuation or bad structure
print("missing quote)

# IndentationError: unexpected indent
 print("extra space")

quizData.question: What type of error does this cause? `print("hello)`
quizData.explanation: The missing closing quote is a syntax error; Python can't parse the line.

slides.title: Your New Superpower 🦸
slides.content:
# Understand Errors = Fix Them Fast

Don't fear red text. It's Python telling you exactly what's wrong. With practice, you'll spot mistakes in seconds.
